exposure: time interval from surgery to conception
cohort: 144 pregnant women, including 48 who underwent LSG within 12 months of pregnancy, 42 who underwent LSG more than 1 year before pregnancy, and 54 obese pregnant women who did not undergo surgery (control group)
finding: Pregnancy within one year after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy is associated with an increased risk of small-for-gestational-age infants, while LSG itself appears to decrease the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus regardless of the time between surgery and conception.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in the rates of cesarean section between women who had pregnancies within 12 months after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy, women who became pregnant more than one year after surgery, and obese pregnant women who did not undergo surgery.
birth_weight: Increased risk of small-for-gestational-age infants in the group who underwent LSG within one year of pregnancy
